{{Short description|Diagonal matrix whose elements are plus or minus 1}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''signature matrix''' is  a [[diagonal matrix]] whose diagonal elements are either 1 or -1, that is, any matrix of the form:<ref>{{citation
 | last = Bapat | first = R. B.
 | doi = 10.1007/978-1-84882-981-7
 | isbn = 978-1-84882-980-0
 | location = London
 | mr = 2797201
 | page = 40
 | publisher = Springer
 | series = Universitext
 | title = Graphs and matrices
 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=w5oXUgN5xw0C&pg=PA40
 | year = 2010}}.</ref>

:<math>A=\begin{pmatrix}
\pm 1   & 0       & \cdots & 0       & 0      \\
0       & \pm 1   & \cdots & 0       & 0      \\
\vdots  & \vdots  & \ddots & \vdots  & \vdots \\
0       & 0       & \cdots & \pm 1   & 0      \\
0       & 0       & \cdots & 0       & \pm 1  
\end{pmatrix}.</math>

==Properties==
Any signature matrix is its own [[inverse matrix|inverse]], hence it is an [[involutory matrix]]. It is consequently a [[square root of a matrix|square root]] of the [[identity matrix]].

Since signature matrices are both [[symmetric matrix|symmetric]] and involutory, they are [[orthogonal matrix|orthogonal]]. Consequently, any [[linear transformation]] corresponding to a signature matrix constitutes an [[isometry]]. Geometrically, signature matrices represent a [[reflection (mathematics)|reflection]] in each of the axes corresponding to the negated rows or columns.

If <math>A</math> is an {{math|{{times|''n''|''n''}}}} signature matrix, then:
*The [[Determinant|determinant]] of <math>A</math> is either 1 or -1 (since it is diagonal), and
*<math>-n \leq \operatorname{tr}(A)\leq n</math> (since the diagonal values are either -1 or 1).
